claim: Sum rules of Szego type on the prime stub chain. Window form is Littlewood's lemma: coefficient side 0 at every stage (checked to 5e-13 for zeta, LIOU, U, THIN, WT, P <= 1e4), bound-state term sum(beta - sigma) is a tail invariant, and the free inequality bounds it from below only. Mean form E + 4 pi delta = log zeta(2 sigma) has three nonnegative terms and returns a density bound. At fixed stage every functional of moduli and phases has the same range and distribution over windows for zeta and U (Kronecker; KS p 0.11 to 0.93). The Simon-Zlatos difference sum converges for zeta on Re s > 0 (3.6358 at 1/2), diverges for random U at 1/2, and converges for THIN on Re s > b/2 with its zero at b; it reads only p > t. The H^2 convergence step loses depth 1/2 (kernel zeta(2 delta)). DH: no chain; its zero appears as B_W = 0.0585171825. No statement about zeros.
errors: Unrefereed. One-delay theorems (Simon-Zlatos, Lukic, Killip-Simon) and Cole-Gamelin recalled, not opened; the dictionary to the multi-delay chain is argued. (KS) limit for THIN argued. HEAT argued, not computed; EA, Beurling, phase-rotated transfer operator, theta^w not run. Residual of the stage phase side after the leading pole term not resolved (about 3e-4). Output files were first written to the repository root by mistake and moved into the lane directory.
surviving: Lemma 5: the difference condition holds for the zeta chain on 1/4 < sigma <= 1/2 where the coefficients are not square-summable (true, without consequence for zeros: THIN). Lemma 6: the l^1/l^2 gap of row Q10 equals the depth 1/2 at which point evaluation on H^2 of the infinite torus becomes bounded.
lesson: A sum-rule device outputs Lieb-Thirring bounds: its coefficient side must vanish to give 'no bound states', and then its limit step is the target. Test a coefficient condition against THIN before reading it as zero information: tail-thin sign changes keep every smoothness-in-delay condition.
